units.title: La langue de la salle de classe

words.eg: You {hand} it in on Friday, not the Friday after.
Nobody {takes notes} by hand any more and everybody says they should.

no.to take note: Au singulier, « take note » veut dire « prends-en bonne note » — ce n’est plus le carnet.

words.eg: Miss two weeks and you never quite {catch up}.
There is a {handout} that answers most of this.
{Swap} papers with the person next to you.
The {deadline} moved twice and nobody told us.
If you are {stuck}, say so early rather than late.
Give me a minute, I will {work} it out.
Both girls are at the local {state school} and happy there.
A {private school} here costs more than most mortgages.
He starts {primary school} in September and cannot wait.
{Secondary school} runs from eleven to sixteen or eighteen.
There are three {terms} and a very long summer.

no.a semester: « Semester » est universitaire et surtout américain ; l’école britannique compte en « terms ».

words.eg: The {head teacher} sends an email every Friday afternoon.
Talk to her {form tutor} before you talk to anyone else.
The {school run} explains the traffic at eight fifteen.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces mots concernent des personnes ou des trajets. Lequel découpe l’année ?
odd.why: Le trimestre est une durée ; les autres sont des gens ou des habitudes.

words.eg: I {sit} the exam in June whether I am ready or not.

no.to pass an exam: « To pass », c’est le réussir. Le passer, simplement, c’est « to sit » ou « to take ».

words.eg: She {passed} first time and told nobody.
You can {fail} the whole thing on the listening alone.
There is a {resit} in September, which costs money.
The {mock} is the one that tells you the truth.
Two weeks of {revision} beats two nights of panic.
The {mark} came back higher than the comments suggested.

no.a note: « Note » en anglais, c’est un mot écrit. La note d’un devoir, c’est « a mark » ou « a grade ».

words.eg: Keep the {certificate}, employers here do ask for it.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces mots viennent après l’épreuve. Lequel vient avant ?
odd.why: On révise avant ; on réussit, on échoue ou on repasse après.

words.eg: Half the city is {undergraduates} from October to June.

words.fr: un étudiant de master ou doctorat
words.eg: The {postgraduate} library is quieter and warmer.
She has a {degree} in something she has never once used.
The nine o’clock {lecture} is half empty by November.

no.a lesson: « Lesson », c’est le cours d’école. À l’université, on parle de « lecture ».

words.eg: The {seminar} is where you actually have to speak.
The {dissertation} eats the whole final year.
Your {tutor} is the person to email when it goes wrong.
{Tuition fees} are why everyone here talks about debt.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces mots sont du travail universitaire. Lequel est de l’argent ?
odd.why: Les frais de scolarité se paient ; le reste se fait.
